page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 6455B processors running at a clock speed of up to 3.9 GHz, providing 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The platform is configured with 1024 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, requiring network storage for persistent volumes, and provides a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark data reflects top-tier multi-threaded compute and data-processing capabilities. The instance delivers a multi-core score of 138225.11 in stress-ng and 21367.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests, aided by advanced instruction extensions including AVX-512, Intel AMX Tile, and AMX INT8. Memory bandwidth registers at 474.63 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 213.9 GB/sec for writes. These memory interfaces support high-throughput operations, evidenced by 149.32 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and top-tier results in PassMark database execution.

The instance delivers high compute efficiency for workloads constrained simultaneously by memory capacity and single-thread execution latency. The principal architectural tradeoff is the absence of local NVMe storage, meaning all disk I/O operations must traverse the network. With its combination of 1024 GB DDR5 RAM, high CPU clock speeds, and 50 Gbps networking, the instance is targeted toward memory-intensive production workloads including relational database management systems, in-memory caches, electronic design automation, real-time analytics, and CPU-based LLM inference.
description: Amazon Web Services r7iz.32xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 6455B processors running at 3.9 GHz on the AWS Nitro System. Built on x86_64 architecture with Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions, the instance supplies 1024 GB of DDR5 memory with an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not bundle local disk storage or discrete GPUs, relying on network-attached storage while maintaining a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier performance across multi-core compute, uncached memory bandwidth, and database workloads, achieving 149.32 million Redis SET operations per second and strong CPU-driven LLM inference throughput. The architecture lacks integrated NVMe drives, but its high memory density and processor clock speeds make it well suited for large in-memory databases, electronic design automation, and intensive real-time analytical processing.
